line: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e6
teaches: Some moves are a choice of MOVE and some are a choice of STRUCTURE, and this pawn is the second kind. Playing it to the sixth rank keeps the centre flexible and the light squares guarded; pushing it a square further seizes space and concedes one square permanently. Neither is better — but pick knowingly, because everything you do for the next twenty moves follows from it.
explains: The pawn steps to e6, covering d5 and f5 — the two squares a knight would love in front of this structure. The centre stays fluid and nothing has been conceded.
